subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Urban Century
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Urban Century.

hook.text: In 1800, only 3% of humans lived in cities. Today it's over 56% — and rising fast.

buildup.text: By 2050, two-thirds of the world's population will live in urban areas.

discovery.text: Cities cover just 3% of Earth's land but produce over 70% of global CO₂ emissions.

twist.text: That concentration is also an opportunity — fixing cities fixes most of the climate problem.

climax.text: The choices cities make in the next decade will shape the climate for centuries.

punchline.text: This is the urban century. How we build cities decides everything.

quiz.question: What share of global CO₂ emissions do cities produce?

details.summary: More than 55 percent of the world's population now lives in cities, and that share is projected to reach 68 percent by 2050. Urbanization concentrates demand for energy, water, and resources, making cities both the primary drivers of emissions and the most important arenas for climate solutions.
details.whyItMatters: Cities produce over 70 percent of global CO2 emissions. How they grow and adapt determines whether the world meets or misses its climate targets.
takeaways: Over 55 percent of humanity already lives in urban areas
Cities generate more than 70 percent of global CO2 emissions
Urban population will add 2.5 billion people by 2050

faq.question: Why do cities produce so much CO2?
faq.answer: Cities concentrate energy-intensive activities: heating and cooling buildings, powering industries, fueling transport, and managing waste. Dense populations demand vast supply chains that extend emissions well beyond city limits through embodied carbon in goods and food.

faq.question: Which regions are urbanizing fastest?
faq.answer: Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia are experiencing the fastest urban growth. Lagos, Dhaka, and Kinshasa are among cities growing most rapidly. Much of this growth is informal, creating urgent challenges for infrastructure and climate adaptation.
